meta.title: Run Configuration
meta.description: Complete reference for the in-game settings screen: every difficulty toggle, range and slider, the trainer-region switches (EX adds Sinnoh through Paldea), the difficulty presets with their forced toggles, and the 0–13 boss difficulty scale. Shared sources are cited from the vanilla working tree; rogue_settings.c and rogue_settings_ui.c are byte-identical on the expansion branch (rogue_strings.h differs only in the version string), and files that differ are cited per branch.

prose.heading: Where you change settings
prose.text: The settings screen is opened from the hub's Config Room and has a top-level Difficulty preset plus four submenus: Edit Difficulty (the fine-grained toggles and the Trainers slider), Adventure (battle format, visible wild Pokémon and experience sharing), Trainers (trainer order and the per-region switches) and Game Modes (Classic, Gauntlet, Fast Path). Settings can only be edited while no run is active — changing anything mid-run is rejected with an error sound. A new run generates its rules from the saved settings when it begins, and changing the game mode updates the stored rules immediately, even from the hub.

prose.heading: The 0–13 difficulty scale
prose.text: Each run climbs a fixed ladder of 14 boss stages, one per difficulty point from 0 to 13: eight gym bosses (0–7), four Elite Four members (8–11) and two champion slots (12–13). Trainer level caps rise with each stage, and key trainers apply their preferred weather as the stage number climbs (from stage 4 with the Trainers slider on Average, from stage 2 on Hard, and always on Brutal — never on Easy). Difficulty 13 — the final champion difficulty — is the highest tier in the game: it is the tier that rules like Gauntlet's forced endgame trainers and endgame route items reference.

prose.heading: Custom difficulty and reward level
prose.text: The four presets (Easy, Average, Hard, Brutal) each force a specific combination of difficulty toggles. The moment you change any of those toggles or the Trainers/Items/Legendaries sliders away from a preset's values, the difficulty is shown as Custom ("Your rules, your way!"). Your rewards are then based on the reward level: the highest preset whose forced toggles you still match exactly and whose slider values you meet at least. The Easy preset is the one true baseline — it forces nothing, so any setting combination is at least as hard as Easy.

records.name: Exp. All
records.description: Controls whether your whole party shares battle experience or only the Pokémon actually in the fight.

values.on: All Pokémon in the party will be awarded Exp. even if they didn't enter the battle.
values.off: Only Pokémon send into battle will be awarded Exp. (Not recommended)

records.description: Whether your Pokémon keep leveling past the per-badge level cap.

values.on: Pokémon can gain levels over the Level Cap. (After the Level Cap, will Level slowly)
values.off: Pokémon will stop gaining lvls once they reach the Level Cap.

records.name: Pokédex Variant
records.menu: Pokédex (unlocked after meeting Pokabbie at the hub's Adventure Entrance)
records.description: Which Pokédex list your in-game Pokédex follows, grouped by region (regional dexes, national dexes per generation, and special extras).

differences.vanilla: Seven variants only: Red/Blue/Yellow, Gold/Silver/Crystal, Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald, National Gen. 1–Gen. 3, and Colosseum + XD. The default is the Gen. 3 national dex.
differences.ex: Thirty-seven variants: the two Rogue dexes (Modern, the default, and Classic Plus), every regional dex up to Paldea, National Gen. 1–Gen. 9, Legends (Arceus, Z-A and Z-A + DLC), Conquest, and Colosseum + XD.

records.name: Difficulty
records.description: The active difficulty preset. Editing any of the preset-controlled difficulty toggles or sliders moves the setting to Custom; the reward level shown next to it is the highest preset your configuration still qualifies for.
records.source: src/data/rogue_strings.h @vanilla L83, L93-97, L114-118 / @origin/expansion L83, L93-97, L114-118; include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L537-545 / @origin/expansion L539-547; src/rogue_settings.c @vanilla L497-549, L600-607 (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Revised Mode
records.description: Enable Pokémon edits, indicated by the revised icon. Revised Typings, Abilities, Moves etc.

optionDescriptions.Enabled in Runs: Changes are only active while on an Adventure. (Can be viewed in the Pokédex)
optionDescriptions.Enabled Always: Changes are always active. This cannot be turned off once Enabled. (Can be viewed in the Pokédex)

records.note: Switching to Enabled Always asks for confirmation: "Are you sure? Your save file will be permanently locked to this setting."
records.source: src/rogue_settings_ui.c @vanilla L439-476 (identical @origin/expansion); include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L621-624 / @origin/expansion L623-626

records.name: Trainer Order
records.description: How the bosses and key trainers are selected as you climb the run's difficulty ladder.

optionDescriptions.Default: Trainers appear somewhat randomly based on their Trainer Class.
optionDescriptions.Rainbow: Trainers appear randomly without repeating types e.g. E4 can be Gyms
optionDescriptions.Official: Trainers appear in the order they appear in official games. (Disables Challenges)

records.note: In Rainbow order, boss trainers of any class (gym, Elite or champion) can appear at any stage, Rogue-region trainers are excluded, and trainers flagged rainbow-excluded are skipped. In Official order the stage is locked to the canonical order (Gym 1, Gym 2, … Elite 4, Champion) and challenge quests are disabled for the run.
records.source: src/rogue_settings_ui.c @vanilla L111-114, L221-242 (identical @origin/expansion); include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L649-652 / @origin/expansion L651-654; src/rogue_trainers.c @vanilla L890, L926-930, L1033-1060 (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_settings.c @vanilla L289-292 (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Easy
records.description: For those who want a casual experience, comparable to modern Pokémon games.
records.note: Easy forces no toggles at all — it is the baseline every configuration qualifies for, so its preset values are recommendations rather than requirements.

records.name: Custom
records.description: Your rules, your way!
records.note: Custom is not a preset you select — it appears whenever your toggles or sliders deviate from every preset's forced values. Your rewards use the highest preset you still match (toggles must match exactly, sliders must be at least that preset's value).
